semantic_units_definition: One unit per: function definition; type definition (struct/enum); arithmetic or comparison operation (including the operation in a compound assignment); local binding (including accumulators); call; conditional (if/else or ternary); loop (init/test/step of a range loop are part of the one loop unit); match (1) plus one per arm; field access; borrow creation (shared or exclusive); read or write through a reference; ownership move (counted even when implicit); early return; result construction (Ok/Err); result propagation (?/try/or_return). Variable references, literals and type annotations count zero. Counted on the language-independent program, so every language variant of a program shares the same value.

A.description: Anchor. Function `f NAME(P:T,..)>U=BODY` (the only currently parsed form), bind `x:=v`, shared borrow `&x`, exclusive borrow `&!x`, implicit move, `match x{..}`, propagation `x?`.

B.description: A with function form `NAME:(P:T,..)>U=BODY` (benchmark-local reading of the matrix entry `f:T>U`; `f` keyword dropped).

D.description: A with exclusive borrow spelled `!&x` (matrix candidate).

E.description: A with keyword bind `let x=v` (matrix verbose reference, whitespace compacted to what the lexer needs).

F.description: A with explicit move sigil `^x` at move sites (matrix candidate `^x`).

G.description: A with compact match `x?{..}` (matrix candidate) instead of `match x{..}`.

variants.notes: The error type is `()` so every language expresses only success-or-failure.
C has no Result type: status code plus out-parameter is the idiomatic equivalent.
Zig error union with `try`; the error carries no payload, matching Rust's `Result<i64, ()>`.
Odin multi-return `(i64, bool)` with `or_return`; the bool stands in for the payload-free error.
